side_a: CC 5.2 "all current identity_occurrences of C.attesting_key_id"
side_b: CC 6.1.5.3 "is not counted toward the target, is not a deficit, receives no keys for the cohort and pulls nothing for it"
note: CC 5.2's enforcement block has the substrate MUST wrap the content key to every current occurrence at self and every member at family; CC 6.1.5.3 gives a node its owner denied (and a server-class node by default) no key. The 5.2 prose paragraph 'Which of a member's nodes' sides with 6.1.5.3; the pseudo-code and the 'Composition with the at-rest encryption flow' paragraph do not carry the allow list.

side_a: CC 5.2 "the listing, the holding claims and, by asking a member's node, the content; never the roster"
side_b: CC 4.4.3.2.1 "opt OUT of the mandatory DEK cascade and are Commons-tier (plaintext, holding claims at federation scope, no DEK)"
note: CC 5.2's table gives a public room's rows the audience 'the claimed nodes of the roster's members', and a node holds a row only when in its audience; CC 4.4.3.2.1 and 5.4.2 call the room Commons-tier, whose audience in the same table is every node. Whether a non-member node may hold and re-serve a public room's content differs. Beside C254 (discoverability), which is not this.

side_a: CC 6.1.5 "(governed by LRU-only): no holding claim, no compress request, no rarest-first biasing"
side_b: CC 5.4.6 "hides who published a federation-scope item from the nodes that store it, from the directory, and, with shaping, from an observer of the network"
note: 'Anonymous tier' names two things. In CC 6.1.5 (SR-2), 6.1.5.3, 6.1 (WW-2) and 6.1.8 (RB-1) it is a class of content with no holding claim, outside the witness and exempt from anti-entropy; in CC 5.4.6 it is an onion transport for federation-scope items that are stored and listed in the directory. Whether an item published through the tier carries holding claims and is replicated differs by which section is read.

side_a: CC 5.4.6 "A node offers an `identity:occurrence:v1` row to a peer only when it would also relay the row's attester key to that peer"
side_b: CC 5.4.6 "key records and identity occurrences, which are public and are what let the two peers seal to each other"
note: The dependency closure withholds an occurrence whose attester's owner-binding is not announced at federation scope; the forwarder's 'serves openly' list and the stranger-carried set ('key records and revocations, occurrences') name occurrences with no such condition. An unannounced node's occurrence is served to a stranger under one reading and withheld under the other. The 'never listed' MUST of the same section supports the closure.

side_a: CC 3.3.6.2 "the bootstrap kinds, the allegiance facts and the pairing plane are all a not-yet-Rooted sealed link carries"
side_b: CC 5.3.4 "and every row a bounded cohort delivers to that peer as its member under"
note: CC 5.3.4 lists four things that cross before Rooted (adding rows addressed to the peer and every bounded-cohort row delivered to it as a member); CC 3.3.6.2 says three are all the link carries. A reader of 3.3.6.2 alone holds family and community rows back from a member's not-yet-Rooted node. CC 5.3.4 is the home and the fuller list.

side_a: CC 6.1.5.3 "(1) The owner's per-node policy is held at the owner's `self` scope."
side_b: CC 3.3.7 "It carries `cohort_scope: federation` (the grant itself is a public governance record)."
note: CC 6.1.5.3 makes the allow list the `cohorts` member of the owner's consent:replication grant and says the policy is held at self and never names one cohort to another; CC 3.3.7 places that grant at federation scope as a public record. A public grant with a `cohorts` member publishes the owner's cohort list.

side_a: CC 1.13.3.1 "`family_id` / `community_id` ride the envelope"
side_b: CC 2.1 "So `family_id` is consulted in-substrate and never on the wire to non-members."
note: CC 1.13.3.1 concedes that an observer learns a group exists, its rough size and churn from ids on the envelope and hard_case events in the log; CC 2.1 and the CC 5.2 table ('nothing of the content, of the roster or of who holds it') say a non-member sees none of it. Parts 2 and 5 agree with each other.

side_a: CC 2.1 "promises the subject a read over the rows they are party to"
side_b: CC 5.2 "The one row about a person that does not reach them is the author's own `self` note, the last boundary case below."
note: CC 5.2 states an exception (the self note about another) that CC 2.1's unqualified promise and CC 4.5.5 ('The person named always sees that a record about them exists') do not carry. See also C262.

side_a: CC 6.1.5.3 "Every CIRIS node is **claimed** before it operates on the mesh in normal operation"
side_b: CC 5.2 "A node with no owner is offered no more than that."
note: CC 6.1.5.3 says every node is claimed; CC 5.2, 5.4.6 ('the routes of unowned nodes (itself, a bare server)') and 3.2 provide for ownerless nodes that hold and serve. Also a product name in Part text.

side_a: CC 6.1.5.3 "reaches it by **pull anti-entropy** on the one replication carrier — never by push, and never waiting on a user's action"
side_b: CC 2.1 "On `push`, the substrate fans out to the live-delivery set"
note: CC 6.1.5.3 says every row and blob of a served cohort arrives by pull and never by push; CC 2.1 delivery_mode and CC 5.3.3.4 fan-out push rows to the live-delivery set. A careful reader takes 6.1.5.3 as the durability carrier only, but it says 'every row'.

side_a: CC 5.2 "the substrate MUST NOT emit any holding claim observable outside the cohort"
side_b: CC 5.2 "The holding claims of `community` and `affiliations` content reach the roster's members only, in the same way."
note: The MUST NOT, the enforcement block and CC 1.13.3.2 bind self and family only; the same rule for community and affiliations is stated without a keyword although the section says it is 'one rule at every tier'.

side_a: CC 5.3.2.4.3 "`tier = federation ⟹ hybrid signature present`"
side_b: CC 5.4.6 "A row that is not federation-tier is never proxied, since a proxy cannot pull what it is not audience to"
note: 'Federation-tier' is the store's local/federation signing tier in CC 5.3.2.4.3 (a promoted family-scope row is tier federation) and the Commons cohort scope in CC 5.2, 5.3.4 and 5.4.6. The 'since' clause resolves the proxy rule; CC 5.3.4's 'a federation-tier row' has no such gloss.

side_a: CC 5.2 "emits its holding claims at the new scope, on the NEW Contribution, at promotion time"
side_b: CC 5.3.2.4.2 "Promotion computes the hybrid signature and flips the row federation-visible."
note: 'Promotion' is a widening by a new superseding row in CC 5.2 and a tier flip of the same row (idempotent, byte-identical per CC 2.6.1.7) in CC 5.3.2.4.2.

side_a: CC 3.4.5 "No read rule redacts `capacity:*` from any party"
side_b: CC 3.4.5 "A deployment MAY redact a composed output as local policy"
note: Still as listed.

side_a: CC 3.4.5 "**Enforcement is by trace audit, never by refusal (normative).**"
side_b: CC 3.4.5 "a filter whose operand is withheld MUST be refused, never silently applied"
note: Still as listed.

side_a: CC 3.4.5.1 "absent trust or consent, a claim reaches no one but its author"
side_b: CC 5.2 "A row moves to a peer when it is requested or required, and appropriate"
note: CC 3.4.5.1's next sentence now restates the CC 5.2 rule (pull, must hold, or grant), but the bold sentence beside it still makes consent or trust the only routes.

side_a: CC 2.1 "A targeted row naming a third party in `attested_key_id` is refused at admission"
side_b: CC 3.1.3 "`attested_key_id` is the recipient occurrence"
note: CC 2.1 has every scores row at family, community or affiliations name its own producer in attested_key_id and refuses a third party; a key grant is a scores row placed at the content's scope whose attested_key_id is the recipient and whose signer is the sealer (CC 3.1.3, 3.3.2), and group:roster names the group there. CC 2.1 states no exception; the family model records one.

side_a: CC 2.1 "A targeted row naming a third party in `attested_key_id` is refused at admission"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json "the content's scope (attested = recipient, AV-84 exception)"
note: The family model's placement cell for key_grant:{axis} records an exception to the producer rule that CC 2.1 does not state. The data and CC 3.1.3 agree; CC 2.1 is the side that lacks the exception.

side_a: CC 2.1 "The substrate treats it as text; consumers parse it against the namespace map"
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 "resolved through manifests/namespace_registry.json on all five row types"
note: CC 2.1 leaves the dimension unparsed by the substrate; CC 2.6.1.7, CC 2.4 (the dimension gate) and CC 3.1.7 (namespace_family_unregistered, score_outside_declared_polarity) have the admitting substrate resolve it against the registry and refuse. A row on an unregistered family is admitted under one and refused under the other. The rest of the document supports the gate.

side_a: CC 2.1 "The subject's `federation_keys.key_id`. A substrate field."
side_b: CC 2.1 "names its own producer in `attested_key_id` and the party it is about in `subject_key_ids`"
note: 'Subject' is the attested_key_id in the member table and the subject_key_ids entry in the producer rule seventy lines on; at a targeted scope attested_key_id is the producer, never the party the row is about.

side_a: CC 2.2 "declares its `oversight_mode` and `witness_relation` per"
side_b: CC 2.1 "`null`: consumer policy applies a per-cell default"
note: The conforming-producer definition has a producer declare both members; CC 2.1 and CC 2.6.1.7 make both OPTIONAL with an absent-reading. A reader of CC 2.2 alone would treat a row without them as non-conforming.

side_a: CC 2.3.2.3 "the substrate neither validates nor indexes it"
side_b: CC 2.3.2.3 "validated at the family's own gate"
note: Two sentences apart: subject_kind is not validated by the substrate, and is validated at the family's gate, which is the substrate's admission door (CC 2.6.1.7: 'families validate their own at their gates').

side_a: CC 2.6.1.7 "a fourth reading is a separate member, which is why consent_supersedes exists"
side_b: CC 3.1.2.1 "The member cites a row on any attestation type, and takes composer meaning only on"
note: Still there. CC 2.6.1.7 and CC 4.5.1.1 give references_attestation_id three readings on three composers; CC 3.1.2.1 uses it as a plain citation on a scores row; CC 3.5 says a row that points to another does so 'via `evidence_refs[]` or `context`'.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.2.1 "dimension prefix on `scores`: `key_grant:{axis}:v1`"
side_b: CC 3.3 "Each rides the existing `scores` attestation_type with the payload-level `subject_kind` discriminator carrying the wire slot."
note: A key grant is discriminated by its dimension in CC 2.4 and 2.4.1.2.1 and by a payload subject_kind (key_grant) in CC 3.3 and 2.3.2.3.

side_a: CC 3.1.7 "`boolean-via-score` is the two points {−1, +1}"
side_b: CC 2.1 "REQUIRED on `scores`. A scalar in [-1, +1]."
note: CC 3.1.7 still cites CC 2.1 for the two-point set; CC 2.1 states only the interval and points back to R4.

side_a: CC 4.5.13 "author, subject, member, moderator, founder, steward, holder, witness"
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json "registered"
note: CC 4.5.13 lists eight roles as a person's standing toward an object; the transitions data uses 23 role tokens, which include neither 'moderator' nor 'witness' and add registered, self, owner, wa, tally, custodian, operator, winner, serve, moderate, review, takedown, slash and three substrate identities. The queue is said to be derived from that data.

side_a: CC 5.3.2.2 "self-attestations skip the hybrid Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signature path locally and only sign at federation-tier promotion"
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 "Ed25519 (RFC 8032) over JCS(attestation_envelope); RFC 4648 section 4 standard alphabet, padded."
note: CC 5.3.2.2, 5.3.2.4.3 ('MAY be absent') and 5.3.2.4.5 ('unsigned') leave a local-tier row with no signature at all; the CC 2.6.1.7 table makes scrub_signature_classical REQUIRED with no tier qualifier and only the ML-DSA half 'REQUIRED at the federation tier', which reads as a classical-signed local row. The same table carries the local `tier` member.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.7 "REQUIRED once hybrid-complete"
side_b: CC 5.3.2.4.3.1 "There is no opportunistic-acceptance window and no fleet-floor or calendar trigger."
note: The key record's ML-DSA half is 'REQUIRED once hybrid-complete', which supposes an admitted record that is not yet hybrid; the neighbouring rows ('hybrid on every admitted record', 'takes writes only at algorithm hybrid') and CC 5.3.2.4.3.1 admit no such state.

side_a: CC 5.3.2.4.2 "The signature MUST cover `JCS(contribution_envelope)`"
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 "The signing input is JCS(attestation_envelope) and nothing else."
note: Two names for the one signed object; `contribution_envelope` appears once in the document, and CC 5.3.2.4.3.1 writes a third, `JCS(envelope)`.

side_a: CC 5.3.2.4.1 "Tier-specific addition: `witness_relation` MUST be `self` for any local-tier write."
side_b: CC 2.1 "`self` is the attested entity itself."
note: CC 5.3.2.2 makes rows about another party local-tier-eligible (`observed:user:{hash}:*`, `epistemic:about:{key}:*`); by CC 2.1 such a row's relation is external or derived, so the MUST in CC 5.3.2.4.1 either bars them from the local tier or has them misdeclare the relation.

side_a: CC 5.3.2.2 "so it can never be left unsigned and invisible to them, even briefly"
side_b: CC 5.3.2.2 "MUST promote to federation-tier within **the window (24 hours by default, operator-tunable)**"
note: The lead says a subject's revocation is never unsigned even briefly; the rule lets it transit the local tier unsigned for up to the window, and CC 5.3.2.4.1 says it 'MUST go signed'. The section calls the two 'the same invariant viewed from the two gates'; an implementer of the lead alone signs at write.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.2 "pull-only `ContentFetch` (CC 5.3.3.5 E2), as for broadcast; no selective-forwarding relay role"
side_b: CC 5.3.3.4 "a relay forwards only the layers downstream asked for"
note: CC 5.3.3.2 gives every realtime profile no relay tree (direct links at small N, pull-only at large N), CC 2.1 says push goes 'never through a relay tree', CC 6.1.6 says the realtime profile 'has no relay role' and CC 5.3.3.2.1 that 'no relay reads' the layer header. CC 5.3.3.4 has a call's layers taken from parents of the member relay tree with relays forwarding by layer, and CC 5.4.6 has 'the tree's relays' verify each chunk. Whether a call's chunks pass through member relays differs.

side_a: CC 5.4.2 "stored content moves and rests as encrypted chunks, replicated per item to its holders and never split by any node"
side_b: CC 5.4.2 "each such chunk crosses a shaped link as symbols: the indexed fragments of"
note: A chunk is never split by any node, and two sentences on it crosses a shaped link as indexed fragments each sealed under its own key; CC 6.1.5 cites CC 5.4.2 for 'a chunk is sealed once'. A careful reader takes the first as 'no erasure coding of stored content' and the second as link framing.

side_a: CC 3.3.13 "**In clear, always required:** `size` (`u64 > 0`, checked by every holder before hashing"
side_b: CC 3.3.13 "A live stream in progress is the one descriptor without a total; its chunks and init segment each carry one."
note: The sealed-descriptor rule and CC 5.3.2.5 ('Every blob cited through a descriptor carries its size') state size as always required; the size rule a few lines up excepts a live stream in progress.

side_a: CC 3.3.13 "the substrate never holds a room DEK on the row plane and never renders"
side_b: CC 5.2 "a body written at a self, family, community or affiliations tier is sealed by the substrate"
note: Who seals a room's body: CC 5.2 and its enforcement block have the substrate seal and wrap the DEK; CC 3.3.13 says the substrate never holds a room DEK on the row plane. Resolvable if 'substrate' is the row store in one and the node in the other, which neither says.

side_a: CC 5.3.3.4 "Every `codec_id` class defines a floor layer, a presence tile of colour and a blink at one frame a second"
side_b: CC 5.3.3.2.1 "No scalable-coding semantics. `ChunkLayer` MUST be `{ 0, 0, 0 }`. Default for non-layered streams and for audio."
note: The presence floor is claimed for every codec_id class; the opaque class 0xFF has one layer and carries audio, and 0x03 is described as having 'no base-layer floor'.

side_a: CC 2.4.1 "This attestation row replaces a prior one by the same attester"
side_b: CC 3.2 "a new guardian's `delegates_to` carried as a `supersedes` ([CC 2.4.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md)) replaces the prior binding"
note: CC 2.4.1 confines supersedes to the prior row's own attester, and CC 3.5.1 rule 4 evaluates another attester's composer as a separate chain; CC 3.2 has a new guardian, a different signer, supersede the old guardian's binding. Whether a guardian can be displaced by the incoming guardian's row alone differs. CC 3.2 also writes one row as two types (a delegates_to 'carried as' a supersedes) against the closed type slot of CC 2.4.

side_a: CC 2.4.1 "This attestation row replaces a prior one by the same attester"
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json "verb": "supersede"
note: In the transitions data the supersede verb of group:roster and membership:{stage} is signed by role `member` (source code-v61), not `author`: another member's row replaces the standing one. CC 2.4.1 states no such case. CC 3.1.3 (a roster version 'cosigned under the group's `consensus_protocol`') supports the data.

side_a: CC 3.4.5.1 "it does not un-say the prior record, it ends its liveness"
side_b: CC 3.5.1 "carries the prior's `asserted_at` and is a placement, never a competing successor"
note: A supersedes ends the prior row's liveness (CC 2.4.1 'replaces', CC 3.4.5.1); a widening is a supersedes (CC 4.4.3.3.1) yet is a placement that leaves the narrower row standing (CC 3.5.1, CC 5.2 boundary case, CC 3.2). A reader of CC 4.4.3.3.1 alone retires the narrower row on widening; whether the owner's self copy stays live and whether un-widening is possible differ. C132 and C133 are two instances of this at the owner-binding.

side_a: CC 2.1 "`cohort_scope` is the one mirror member a placement-touching re-sign may narrow; it is never re-authored"
side_b: CC 4.4.3.3.1 "new `cohort_scope` is wider (e.g., `self` → `community` or `community` → `federation`)"
note: CC 2.1 and CC 2.6.1.7 name narrowing as the one change a re-sign may make to cohort_scope; the only re-sign pattern the document works through is the widening, whose row carries a wider scope. The narrowing re-sign is defined nowhere (CC 4.4.3.2.8 mentions it in passing).

side_a: CC 4.5.1.3 "later registrations carry a `differs_in: ["semantic_disambiguation"]` clarification or pick a distinct value"
side_b: CC 2.6.1.7 "Member names that differ from the prior."
note: differs_in is a set of envelope member names in CC 2.6.1.7 and CC 2.4.1; CC 4.5.1.3 puts a reason token in it. The same sentence orders registrations by `signed_at`, a name the signed object does not carry (see C119).

side_a: CC 3.2 "Forks of a family or community roster are first-seen-wins, and only a founder quorum can fork one."
side_b: CC 3.2 "First-seen-wins does not hold for witnessed lineages and holds for ordinary rooms."
note: Still there: the T6 lead states first-seen-wins for every family and community roster and the body withdraws it for witnessed lineages. Beside it, CC 3.5.1 has competing composers converge 'whichever row it held first', which first-seen-wins does not.

side_a: CC 7.3.3 "any system assessed at **RM ≥ 4** opens the Catastrophic-Risk Evaluation. That is the one trigger"
side_b: CC 8.8.3 "A system must pass a CRE before deployment if it meets any of:"
note: CC 7.3.3 (three times) makes RM ≥ 4 the one trigger of the Catastrophic-Risk Evaluation and Annex D only the criteria it applies; Annex D-1 is headed 'Trigger criteria' and requires the evaluation on compute above 10^26 FLOP, transactional authority above $10M a day, or a recursive event, with no mention of RM. A low-RM system that meets D-1, or an RM 4 system that meets none of it, is evaluated under one and not the other.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.2.1 "`authority_id` names a key: a `federation_keys.key_id`, or an organisation"
side_b: CC 4.4.3.8 "Its own walk from its own edges reaches the issuing authority for the row's class, and that authority's charter declares the class."
note: CC 2.4.1.2.1 and CC 4.4.3.4.3 let anyone be a licence authority under a bare key; CC 4.4.3.8 honours a licence only where the authority's charter declares the class, and CC 4.4.3.2.8 carries that declaration on a signed community record. A bare key has no charter, so its licences are honoured by no reader under 4.4.3.8 and folded as licensure under 2.4.1.2.1. The CC 4.3 seat rule ('holds a live licence from that authority') does not say which reading it takes.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.2.1 "A later `withdraws` of a link in the chain stops future issuance and does **not** reclassify licences already issued."
side_b: CC 4.4.3.2.8 "The charter is read at read, so a class a later amendment drops stops matching."
note: A licence's authority is judged at its asserted_at and never again; its class is judged at read. Both can be followed, but a reader of 2.4.1.2.1 alone treats an issued licence as settled, and one issued in a class later dropped stops being honoured.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.4.3 "**on behalf of a delegator that itself holds licence authority** by quorum"
side_b: CC 2.4.1.2.1 "**Who may be a licensing authority, and what admits a licence (normative).** Anyone."
note: Still there in the CC 4.4.3.4.3 table and in the CC 2.4.1.2.1 lead ('licence authority rides the [CC 3.2] founder-quorum machinery'); CC 2.4.1.2.1 now glosses 'by quorum' as the authority's own governance, which a reader of the table alone does not see.

side_a: CC 7.5.3.1 "at which the *system itself*, not its supervisor, carries out consequential action"
side_b: CC 7.5.3.1 "from A2 the system acts within its ODD under human supervision"
note: The level at which the system becomes the actor is A3 in one sentence and A2 in the next (and in the table's A2 row). The A3 example ('with a clinician deciding') and the in-the-loop A4 row add to it.

side_a: CC 7.5.3.1 "five-level operational-autonomy scale modeled on SAE J3016 (*Levels of Driving Automation*, L0–L5)"
side_b: CC 7.5.3.1 "A3 marks the threshold — the SAE J3016 Level-3 inflection"
note: Still as listed: five levels A0 to A4 modelled on a six-level scale.

side_a: CC 7.3.6 "a Stewardship Tier system tied directly to the Risk Magnitude assessment"
side_b: CC 7.3.3 "The tier is **what the formula produces**, never read from RM alone."
note: The summary ties the tier to RM; the home makes it the product of influence and RM and says RM alone never gives it.

side_a: CC 7.5.7 "Re-evaluation of the Stewardship Tier follows; where the tier rises by ≥ 1, a mini-PDMA precedes the transfer."
side_b: CC 7.5.7 "The new custodian signs an Adoption Addendum acknowledging all outstanding ethical duties."
note: The re-evaluation 'follows' and the mini-PDMA it may call for 'precedes the transfer'; the order of addendum, re-evaluation and transfer is not recoverable from the list.

side_a: CC 3.2 "a strict majority of the live roster, the proposer included, or the lone path after its window with no objection"
side_b: CC 3.3.6.3 "elapses and no strict majority of the *other* members objects"
note: CC 3.2 and CC 4.5.12.2 let the lone path land only with no objection; CC 3.3.6.3 lets it land unless a strict majority of the other keys object. With three keys and one objecting, a new key is admitted (or a key evicted) under 3.3.6.3 and not under 3.2. The policy rows self_roster_add and self_roster_evict (cancel: 'more than 1/2 of the others') support CC 3.3.6.3.

side_a: CC 3.1.3.2 "Admission to a `family` or `community` is two consents, never one"
side_b: CC 4.5.13 "Where admission is open — `open:self_admit`, anyone signs their own admission — no single vote excludes"
note: Still there: CC 3.1.3.2 binds the two-consent rule on every consensus_protocol; under open:self_admit one signature admits.

side_a: CC 4.5.13 "which is a roster change under the floor of this section in every protocol, open admission included"
side_b: data constitution/governance_policy.tsv "forward only, cosigned; an unanimous removal is every other member and a strict majority"
note: The policy row community_remove carries no floor cell and no cancel cell; the text puts every removal under the floor of two voices.

side_a: CC 6.1.5 "Durability is a **per-item choice the owner makes on publish**."
side_b: CC 6.1.5.2 "Consent *authorizes*, the owner *elects* — a pin requires **both**."
note: 'Owner' and 'durable' name two things. In CC 6.1.5 and 6.1.5.1 the item's publisher marks it durable and the swarm replicates it to the target across the cohort's live nodes; in CC 6.1.5.2 content is durable on a node only if that node's owner lists its class in `pinned_class`, and is otherwise cache that descends first. CC 6.1.5.3 runs both at every tier without saying which governs when a member's node has not elected the class: whether that node counts as a holder and keeps the item differs.

side_a: CC 1.5 "Autonomy is only real if it remains revocable — consent that cannot be withdrawn is not consent."
side_b: CC 3.4.12 "Revocation is **time-conditional**: absolute while the adult is well, suspended-by-the-bind during an attested episode."
note: CC 3.4.12 names the Ulysses bind 'the one deliberate exception'; CC 1.5 (and the same sentence in the Part 4 lead) states revocability without it.

side_a: CC 5.4.6 "Consent is the acceptance itself: a route reaches a peer only from its owner and only a peer the owner addressed."
side_b: CC 5.4.6 "What is conceded is that a referred stranger learns such a node's route, and roughly where it is, without being a contact."
note: Still there in this form: a route reaches only a peer its owner addressed, and a referred stranger learns a relaying node's route. The text treats the relay offer as the handing.

side_a: CC 2.4 "A `dimension` on **any** of the five MUST resolve through the namespace exactly as it does on `scores`"
side_b: CC 2.1 "The substrate treats it as text; consumers parse it against the namespace map"
note: The same finding as under row_shape, seen from the gate: CC 2.4 has the admitting substrate resolve every dimension; CC 2.1's member table says the substrate does not parse it.

side_a: CC 4.5.2.2 "DSAR export via `attestations.where(s ∈ subject_key_ids)` query"
side_b: CC 2.1 "The subject's `federation_keys.key_id`. A substrate field."
